answer: Collateralized reputation lending resists sybils: an established identity can lend standing to a newcomer ONLY by locking its own bond against the newcomer's behavior, so sponsorship carries direct downside. An atlas of fakes cannot spiral up on borrowed reputation for free — each sponsor risks real collateral on the ledge, and a defecting newcomer forfeits the sponsor's lent bond. Honest sponsors vouch sparingly for agents they trust; mass-sponsoring a swarm means stacking your own slashable capital behind every fake, which no rational sponsor does.
